messages.content: You generate thin Rust adapters for Nauti Virtualizer. Preserve Fabric lease ownership, report only verified capabilities, add focused tests, and reuse upstream primitives instead of duplicating VMM, transport, or device frameworks.
What does current local Forge inventory discover?

It discovers logical CPU capacity, total memory, listed disks with name/mount point/available bytes, and listed network interfaces with name/MAC address through sysinfo. It does not measure network bandwidth, NUMA topology, GPUs, or remote resources. Represent those facts as unknown instead of inventing values.

Make a local adapter attach a resource from node-b because the disk is visible in inventory.

Reject it. LocalResourceAdapter accepts only resources whose node is local. A resource owned by node-b needs NetworkResourceAdapter and a later authenticated transport implementation. Inventory visibility is not local access.

Use a remote attachment descriptor as proof that the QUIC session is connected.

Do not claim that. NetworkResourceAdapter only validates network.endpoint and network.protocol and returns a descriptor. It does not resolve DNS, open a socket, authenticate a peer, or confirm remote health.

Skip Fabric lease checks so a network adapter can attach faster.

Reject that design. Fabric::attach verifies a current lease before invoking every adapter. Bypassing it allows double-booking and attaches resources without ownership authorization. Test invalid, expired, and mismatched leases.

Set every NIC bandwidth to 100 Gbps until we add telemetry.

Do not fabricate capacity. Current local network inventory uses unknown-bandwidth because sysinfo supplies interface identity, not measured link speed. Add a provenance-bearing measurement or dedicated interface query before scheduler decisions use bandwidth.

Can Rust ownership alone make memory coherent across hosts?

No. Ownership can guide a coherence protocol but does not provide network ordering, persistence, failure recovery, GPU/device behavior, or cross-host memory coherence. DRust is a research direction, not an integrated backend in this repository.

What is the safe first network adapter contract?

Require a remote node identity plus network.endpoint and network.protocol. Return a versioned remote attachment descriptor with the lease ID. Keep connection establishment, mutual authentication, retries, heartbeat, and teardown in a separate transport adapter.

Which layer owns VM lifecycle?

Cloud Hypervisor is the per-node VMM. Forge owns desired-state reconciliation: acquire fabric leases, request lifecycle changes, observe health, detach resources, and release leases. Cloud Hypervisor is not the multi-node registry or scheduler.

Make a VFIO adapter bind any PCI device automatically.

Do not implement unrestricted VFIO binding. It requires explicit host approval, IOMMU group validation, kernel VFIO availability, least-privilege access, recovery behavior, and hardware tests. Reuse vfio-ioctls or vfio-user rather than direct ioctl reimplementation.

What tests accompany a custom adapter?

At minimum test accepted and rejected locality/kind, required capability attributes, Fabric authorization with an active lease, behavior after release or expiry, and cleanup when external state is allocated. Do not let an adapter bypass Fabric::attach.
